request.note: The server uses the first 15 entries and ignores the rest. An entry that is a number or a string reads as `{}` and gets `"no_item"`. A `null` entry throws.

confirm.note: Of each entry the handler reads `num` and `slot`. Setting `.num` on a number or string entry does nothing (no strict mode), so `num` reads `undefined` and the slot is empty

responses.name: Success
responses.when: The payload is an array. The server equips the entries in order and stops at the first entry that fails. It sends this reply also when an entry failed: the code of that entry is the last element of `slots`.

fields.name: slots
fields.description: One element for each entry that the server read: a result for each equipped entry, then the code of the first failed entry (if any). `invalid`: `num` is past the end of the inventory. `no_item`: the slot is empty. `item_blocked`: the item has the flag `b`. `item_placeholder`: an upgrade or compound runs on the slot. `cant_equip`: `can_equip_item` refuses the item for the slot.

failures.intro: A failure of one entry is not in this table: it is the last element of `slots` in the success reply.

rows.when: The payload is not an array. The server stopped your channeled actions (`c`) already.
An entry is `null`, or the item in its slot has a name that is not in `G.items`. The handler throws. The entries before it stay equipped, and the server sends no `player` update.

also.when: An entry gets `cant_equip`, its slot is `weapon`, `mainhand` or `tool`, you hold an offhand item, and the item is a two-handed weapon for your class.

example.message: Unequip your offhand item to use this two-handed weapon.

also.summary: Your state with `reopen: true`, the new `slots` and `items`, the recalculated stats, and the `penalty_cd` condition in `s`.

order: `game_log` to you, only for a two-handed weapon that your offhand item blocks
